acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Structured JSON logging with timestamp, correlation ID, method, path, status, latency
No PII or sensitive data in logs (API keys, auth tokens, passwords)
Log levels configurable via LOG_LEVEL environment variable
GET /metrics exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics (request count, latency histograms, error rates)
GET /health returns detailed status with services breakdown and version
Startup logs include version, environment, and configuration summary
X-Request-ID correlation ID in response headers

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: NFR-O1 through NFR-O6 detail structured logging with Pino, request correlation IDs, Prometheus metrics endpoint, and health check requirements. Logs must be JSON format with timestamp, level, requestId, message fields.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Observability requirements including structured logging, Prometheus metrics, and monitoring alerting baseline for production operations.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Pino for structured JSON logging, prom-client for Prometheus metrics, request correlation via X-Request-ID headers for distributed tracing.

artifact.reason: Main application setup with existing Pino logger configuration, genReqId for correlation IDs, error handler. This is where metrics plugin will be registered and logging enhanced.
Reference implementation for Fastify plugin pattern using fp() wrapper, addHook for request lifecycle, and decorateRequest. Follow this pattern for metrics.ts.
Another plugin pattern reference showing global middleware registration and configuration via environment variables.
LOG_LEVEL already defined in EnvironmentConfig interface. Use this for log level configuration. Returns env.LOG_LEVEL which can be used in Pino config.
Database health check implementation. Use healthCheck() method pattern for observability checks.
Integration test patterns using app.inject() for HTTP testing. Follow same patterns for metrics and observability tests.
Testing pattern for Fastify plugins. Use similar approach for metrics plugin tests.

constraints.constraint: Logs MUST write to stdout only (no file-based logging per 12-factor app)
NO PII or sensitive data in logs - use Pino redaction for authorization headers, passwords, api keys
Metrics endpoint MUST be Prometheus-compatible (text/plain format)
Log levels configurable at runtime via LOG_LEVEL environment variable
Health check must respond in less than 100ms (NFR-P1)
Use fastify-plugin wrapper (fp) for proper encapsulation
New plugin at apps/api/src/plugins/metrics.ts following auth.ts pattern
Integration tests required for all ACs using Vitest and app.inject()

interface.name: GET /health
interface.signature: GET /health -> JSON { status, timestamp, services, version }

tests.standards: Vitest for test framework with integration tests using Fastify's app.inject() method for HTTP testing without starting server. Tests located in apps/api/src/__tests__/ directory. Follow existing patterns from fastify.test.ts, auth-plugin.test.ts, rate-limit.test.ts. Mock database and external services as needed. Use beforeEach/afterEach for setup/teardown. Test files should be named descriptively: metrics.test.ts, observability.test.ts.

ideas.idea: Test that requests generate structured JSON logs with all required fields (timestamp, reqId, method, url, statusCode, responseTime)
Test that authorization headers and sensitive fields are redacted from logs (check log output does not contain actual API keys)
Test that LOG_LEVEL environment variable controls which log levels are output (set to warn, verify no info logs)
Test GET /metrics returns Content-Type: text/plain with Prometheus format containing http_requests_total and http_request_duration_seconds
Test that metrics increment correctly after requests (make N requests, check counter value)
Test GET /health returns status, timestamp, services.database, and version fields
Test startup logs include application version and NODE_ENV
Verify logs use stdout transport (check logger configuration)
Test all responses include X-Request-ID header matching request.id
Test correlation ID appears in both request log and response header
